# 5.1 · Softmax and Friends

`Level 5: Attention Is Weighted Averages` · `+15 XP` · `drill 1 of 3`

## The job
Write the numerically careful softmax family. `softmax(xs, temperature)` turns scores into
probabilities without overflowing on scores like 1000. `logsumexp(xs)` computes
log(sum(exp(x))) safely. `log_softmax(xs)` returns log probabilities that stay finite
where `log(softmax(xs))` would hit log(0). `cross_entropy(logits, target)` is the loss
for the correct class index.

## Why it matters
Every classifier and every language model ends in exactly these functions, and the naive
versions break the moment a logit gets large. Temperature is also the first knob anyone
turns on a chat model, so it helps to know it is just a division before the softmax.

## Run it

```bash
python fullsend.py check 5.1     # judge your drill.py
python fullsend.py hint 5.1      # one hint at a time
```

<details><summary>All hints (try the drill first)</summary>

1. Subtracting the maximum from every score before exponentiating changes nothing mathematically and prevents overflow.
2. logsumexp(xs) = m + log(sum(exp(x - m))) where m = max(xs).
3. log_softmax(xs)[i] = xs[i] - logsumexp(xs). No exp of a big number, no log of zero.
4. Cross-entropy for one example is minus the log probability of the target: use log_softmax, not log of softmax.
5. Divide by the temperature first; a temperature of zero or below is a ValueError.

</details>
